features.summary: Firefox is integrating Skrifa, a modern font library, deeper into its text rendering pipeline to handle font metrics, character tables, and font names more efficiently. features.summary: Firefox's GPU-accelerated rendering engine received substantial improvements to how it draws shapes, text, and gradients. A major change adds support for CSS corner-shape, which lets web designers create smoothly-curved and fluid borders beyond the traditional rounded rectangles—the engine now uses a mathematical curve called a superellipse to render these shapes efficiently. Behind the scenes, the rendering architecture was significantly refactored, including removal of legacy gradient infrastructure and a shift toward more efficient buffering and transformation handling that **improves performance and reduces memory usage** for complex scenes.

Firefox now supports fractional SVG viewports so SVGs scale more precisely, and image progress notifications are delivered per-observer to make incremental loading and cache behavior more efficient. The JPEG path was updated to use a new CMYK swizzle approach, improving color fidelity for CMYK JPEGs used in print and photography. A few small internal cleanups and default operator-equality changes were also applied (_mostly maintenance, no visible change_).

features.summary: This work adds thorough correctness tests and gtest performance benchmarks around CMYK “swizzling” (the process of rearranging and converting CMYK print colors to display formats) and cleans up platform defines for Android. It also fixes a color-management bug where 16-bit float color data (f16) was being prematurely reduced to 8‑bit (u8) before going through qcms’s tetrahedral CLUT (a color lookup table used for accurate color transforms), which could lose precision. Together these changes give Firefox more reliable and measurable color conversions — especially important for images, printing, and any content where color fidelity matters — and make regressions easier to catch in future.

Specifically, the addition of `qcms_profile_create_cicp_with_intent` enables improved handling of color data in various media formats, ensuring that colors appear more accurately and consistently across different devices. This is particularly important for professionals working in photography and design, as it helps maintain color fidelity when sharing images online. **This means users can expect a more accurate representation of colors in their web content, enhancing the overall visual experience.**

This change is significant as it streamlines the integration between Rust and C languages, improving performance and maintaining a smoother user experience when rendering fonts on webpages. **This means that users can expect better text display and performance across sites that utilize complex font styling.**

features.summary: IPC (IPDL) actor de‑virtualization logic was unified and made stricter about type qualification, which cleans up the interprocess communication code used by VR/AR features.
